paragraphs.text: And he said also unto the disciples, There was a certain rich man, who had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he was wasting his goods.
paragraphs.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς· Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ὃς εἶχεν οἰκονόμον, καὶ οὗτος διεβλήθη αὐτῷ ὡς διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Elegen de kai pros tous mathētas· Anthrōpos tis ēn plousios hos eichen oikonomon, kai houtos dieblēthē autō hōs diaskorpizōn ta hyparchonta autou.

paragraphs.text: And he called him, and said unto him, What is this that I hear of thee? render the account of thy stewardship; for thou canst be no longer steward.
paragraphs.original: καὶ φωνήσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί τοῦτο ἀκούω περὶ σοῦ; ἀπόδος τὸν λόγον τῆς οἰκονομίας σου, οὐ γὰρ δύνῃ ἔτι οἰκονομεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai phōnēsas auton eipen autō· Ti touto akouō peri sou; apodos ton logon tēs oikonomias sou, ou gar dynē eti oikonomein.

paragraphs.text: And the steward said within himself, What shall I do, seeing that my lord taketh away the stewardship from me? I have not strength to dig; to beg I am ashamed.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὁ οἰκονόμος· Τί ποιήσω ὅτι ὁ κύριός μου ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν οἰκονομίαν ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ; σκάπτειν οὐκ ἰσχύω, ἐπαιτεῖν αἰσχύνομαι·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de en heautō ho oikonomos· Ti poiēsō hoti ho kyrios mou aphaireitai tēn oikonomian apʼ emou; skaptein ouk ischyō, epaitein aischynomai·

paragraphs.text: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
paragraphs.original: ἔγνων τί ποιήσω, ἵνα ὅταν μετασταθῶ ἐκ τῆς οἰκονομίας δέξωνταί με εἰς τοὺς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: egnōn ti poiēsō, hina hotan metastathō ek tēs oikonomias dexōntai me eis tous oikous heautōn.

paragraphs.text: And calling to him each one of his lord`s debtors, he said to the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα ἕκαστον τῶν χρεοφειλετῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἑαυτοῦ ἔλεγεν τῷ πρώτῳ· Πόσον ὀφείλεις τῷ κυρίῳ μου;
paragraphs.translit: kai proskalesamenos hena hekaston tōn chreopheiletōn tou kyriou heautou elegen tō prōtō· Poson opheileis tō kyriō mou;

paragraphs.text: And he said, A hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bond, and sit down quickly and write fifty.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν βάτους ἐλαίου· ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ καθίσας ταχέως γράψον πεντήκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Hekaton batous elaiou· ho de eipen autō· Dexai sou ta grammata kai kathisas tacheōs grapson pentēkonta.

paragraphs.text: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, A hundred measures of wheat. He saith unto him, Take thy bond, and write fourscore.
paragraphs.original: ἔπειτα ἑτέρῳ εἶπεν· Σὺ δὲ πόσον ὀφείλεις; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν κόρους σίτου· λέγει αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ γράψον ὀγδοήκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: epeita heterō eipen· Sy de poson opheileis; ho de eipen· Hekaton korous sitou· legei autō· Dexai sou ta grammata kai grapson ogdoēkonta.

paragraphs.text: And his lord commended the unrighteous steward because he had done wisely: for the sons of this world are for their own generation wiser than the sons of the light.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπῄνεσεν ὁ κύριος τὸν οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας ὅτι φρονίμως ἐποίησεν· ὅτι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου φρονιμώτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ φωτὸς εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν εἰσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai epēnesen ho kyrios ton oikonomon tēs adikias hoti phronimōs epoiēsen· hoti hoi hyioi tou aiōnos toutou phronimōteroi hyper tous hyious tou phōtos eis tēn genean tēn heautōn eisin.

paragraphs.text: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends by means of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when it shall fail, they may receive you into the eternal tabernacles.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσατε φίλους ἐκ τοῦ μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας, ἵνα ὅταν ἐκλίπῃ δέξωνται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς.
paragraphs.translit: kai egō hymin legō, heautois poiēsate philous ek tou mamōna tēs adikias, hina hotan eklipē dexōntai hymas eis tas aiōnious skēnas.

paragraphs.text: He that is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much: and he that is unrighteous in a very little is unrighteous also in much.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ ἄδικος καὶ ἐν πολλῷ ἄδικός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: Ho pistos en elachistō kai en pollō pistos estin, kai ho en elachistō adikos kai en pollō adikos estin.

paragraphs.text: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true [riches]?
paragraphs.original: εἰ οὖν ἐν τῷ ἀδίκῳ μαμωνᾷ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἀληθινὸν τίς ὑμῖν πιστεύσει;
paragraphs.translit: ei oun en tō adikō mamōna pistoi ouk egenesthe, to alēthinon tis hymin pisteusei;

paragraphs.text: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another`s, who will give you that which is your own?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ ἐν τῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ὑμέτερον τίς δώσει ὑμῖν;
paragraphs.translit: kai ei en tō allotriō pistoi ouk egenesthe, to hymeteron tis dōsei hymin;

paragraphs.text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
paragraphs.original: οὐδεὶς οἰκέτης δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
paragraphs.translit: oudeis oiketēs dynatai dysi kyriois douleuein· ē gar ton hena misēsei kai ton heteron agapēsei, ē henos anthexetai kai tou heterou kataphronēsei. ou dynasthe theō douleuein kai mamōna.

paragraphs.text: And the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things; and they scoffed at him.
paragraphs.original: Ἤκουον δὲ ταῦτα πάντα οἱ Φαρισαῖοι φιλάργυροι ὑπάρχοντες, καὶ ἐξεμυκτήριζον αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkouon de tauta panta hoi Pharisaioi philargyroi hyparchontes, kai exemyktērizon auton.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Ye are they that justify yourselves in the sight of men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ δικαιοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁ δὲ θεὸς γινώσκει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν· ὅτι τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλὸν βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois· Hymeis este hoi dikaiountes heautous enōpion tōn anthrōpōn, ho de theos ginōskei tas kardias hymōn· hoti to en anthrōpois hypsēlon bdelygma enōpion tou theou.

paragraphs.text: The law and the prophets [were] until John: from that time the gospel of the kingdom of God is preached, and every man entereth violently into it.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται μέχρι Ἰωάννου· ἀπὸ τότε ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται καὶ πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται.
paragraphs.translit: Ho nomos kai hoi prophētai mechri Iōannou· apo tote hē basileia tou theou euangelizetai kai pas eis autēn biazetai.

paragraphs.text: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than for one tittle of the law to fall.
paragraphs.original: Εὐκοπώτερον δέ ἐστιν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν παρελθεῖν ἢ τοῦ νόμου μίαν κεραίαν πεσεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Eukopōteron de estin ton ouranon kai tēn gēn parelthein ē tou nomou mian keraian pesein.

paragraphs.text: Every one that putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and he that marrieth one that is put away from a husband committeth adultery.
paragraphs.original: Πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμῶν ἑτέραν μοιχεύει, καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς γαμῶν μοιχεύει.
paragraphs.translit: Pas ho apolyōn tēn gynaika autou kai gamōn heteran moicheuei, kai ho apolelymenēn apo andros gamōn moicheuei.

paragraphs.text: Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, faring sumptuously every day:
paragraphs.original: Ἄνθρωπος δέ τις ἦν πλούσιος, καὶ ἐνεδιδύσκετο πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον εὐφραινόμενος καθʼ ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς.
paragraphs.translit: Anthrōpos de tis ēn plousios, kai enedidysketo porphyran kai bysson euphrainomenos kathʼ hēmeran lamprōs.

paragraphs.text: and a certain beggar named Lazarus was laid at his gate, full of sores,
paragraphs.original: πτωχὸς δέ τις ὀνόματι Λάζαρος ἐβέβλητο πρὸς τὸν πυλῶνα αὐτοῦ εἱλκωμένος
paragraphs.translit: ptōchos de tis onomati Lazaros ebeblēto pros ton pylōna autou heilkōmenos

paragraphs.text: and desiring to be fed with the [crumbs] that fell from the rich man`s table; yea, even the dogs come and licked his sores.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τοῦ πλουσίου· ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ κύνες ἐρχόμενοι ἐπέλειχον τὰ ἕλκη αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai epithymōn chortasthēnai apo tōn piptontōn apo tēs trapezēs tou plousiou· alla kai hoi kynes erchomenoi epeleichon ta helkē autou.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and that he was carried away by the angels into Abraham`s bosom: and the rich man also died, and was buried.
paragraphs.original: ἐγένετο δὲ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πτωχὸν καὶ ἀπενεχθῆναι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς τὸν κόλπον Ἀβραάμ· ἀπέθανεν δὲ καὶ ὁ πλούσιος καὶ ἐτάφη.
paragraphs.translit: egeneto de apothanein ton ptōchon kai apenechthēnai auton hypo tōn angelōn eis ton kolpon Abraam· apethanen de kai ho plousios kai etaphē.

paragraphs.text: And in Hades he lifted up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, ὑπάρχων ἐν βασάνοις, ὁρᾷ Ἀβραὰμ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ Λάζαρον ἐν τοῖς κόλποις αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai en tō hadē eparas tous ophthalmous autou, hyparchōn en basanois, hora Abraam apo makrothen kai Lazaron en tois kolpois autou.

paragraphs.text: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am in anguish in this flame.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὸς φωνήσας εἶπεν· Πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἐλέησόν με καὶ πέμψον Λάζαρον ἵνα βάψῃ τὸ ἄκρον τοῦ δακτύλου αὐτοῦ ὕδατος καὶ καταψύξῃ τὴν γλῶσσάν μου, ὅτι ὀδυνῶμαι ἐν τῇ φλογὶ ταύτῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai autos phōnēsas eipen· Pater Abraam, eleēson me kai pempson Lazaron hina bapsē to akron tou daktylou autou hydatos kai katapsyxē tēn glōssan mou, hoti odynōmai en tē phlogi tautē.

paragraphs.text: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and Lazarus in like manner evil things: but now here he is comforted and thou art in anguish.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ Ἀβραάμ· Τέκνον, μνήσθητι ὅτι ἀπέλαβες τὰ ἀγαθά σου ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου, καὶ Λάζαρος ὁμοίως τὰ κακά· νῦν δὲ ὧδε παρακαλεῖται σὺ δὲ ὀδυνᾶσαι.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de Abraam· Teknon, mnēsthēti hoti apelabes ta agatha sou en tē zōē sou, kai Lazaros homoiōs ta kaka· nyn de hōde parakaleitai sy de odynasai.

paragraphs.text: And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that they that would pass from hence to you may not be able, and that none may cross over from thence to us.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις μεταξὺ ἡμῶν καὶ ὑμῶν χάσμα μέγα ἐστήρικται, ὅπως οἱ θέλοντες διαβῆναι ἔνθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς μὴ δύνωνται, μηδὲ ἐκεῖθεν πρὸς ἡμᾶς διαπερῶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai en pasi toutois metaxy hēmōn kai hymōn chasma mega estēriktai, hopōs hoi thelontes diabēnai enthen pros hymas mē dynōntai, mēde ekeithen pros hēmas diaperōsin.

paragraphs.text: And he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father`s house;
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δέ· Ἐρωτῶ σε οὖν, πάτερ, ἵνα πέμψῃς αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου,
paragraphs.translit: eipen de· Erōtō se oun, pater, hina pempsēs auton eis ton oikon tou patros mou,

paragraphs.text: for I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.
paragraphs.original: ἔχω γὰρ πέντε ἀδελφούς, ὅπως διαμαρτύρηται αὐτοῖς, ἵνα μὴ καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς βασάνου.
paragraphs.translit: echō gar pente adelphous, hopōs diamartyrētai autois, hina mē kai autoi elthōsin eis ton topon touton tēs basanou.

paragraphs.text: But Abraham saith, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
paragraphs.original: λέγει δὲ Ἀβραάμ· Ἔχουσι Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς προφήτας· ἀκουσάτωσαν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: legei de Abraam· Echousi Mōysea kai tous prophētas· akousatōsan autōn.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one go to them from the dead, they will repent.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Οὐχί, πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἀλλʼ ἐάν τις ἀπὸ νεκρῶν πορευθῇ πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετανοήσουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Ouchi, pater Abraam, allʼ ean tis apo nekrōn poreuthē pros autous metanoēsousin.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, if one rise from the dead.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Εἰ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἀκούουσιν, οὐδʼ ἐάν τις ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ πεισθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de autō· Ei Mōyseōs kai tōn prophētōn ouk akouousin, oudʼ ean tis ek nekrōn anastē peisthēsontai.
